Eligibility Criteria a) Academic Qualification You are eligible to apply if you: • Have passed HSC II /Equivalent with the required minimum percentage, OR • Are currently registered for HSC-II / Equivalent Final / Improvement exams 2026, provided you meet the minimum % requirement. • Combined or accelerated will be considered for available programs after Results. • A current Admit Card or Statement of Entry is mandatory to submit. • Admission will be provisional until final results are submitted and eligibility is confirmed within the deadline. • Pre-medical students can apply to all Engineering, Computing, and Technology programs but must complete a Math deficiency course. General Science students can also apply to all Engineering programs with a mandatory Chemistry deficiency course for confirmation of admission. • Applicants from equivalent boards must submit an IBCC equivalence certificate. b) Important Instructions (Read all carefully) • Check your registered email (Inbox, Junk, or Spam) for registration details • Upload the paid voucher in image format on the portal. Payments near the deadline may take 2–3 working days to verify, while PAYPRO payments are auto-verified. • IBFT and Easypaisa are not allowed, if used, verification from the Accounts Office is required. Upload verified IBFT receipts with your application number on the portal. Visit the Admissions office with paid receipt for assistance. • Check the portal regularly for payment status (in the Progress Tab), test schedule, and updates. • Admit cards are issued a day before the test begins only after fee verification. • The Test Schedule is posted a day or two before the test series starts on both the admissions portal and the official website. Since updates are frequent, check both platforms regularly. If your application number is missing in the test schedule, visit the Admissions Office with your paid voucher for scheduling. On-campus payment is available on test day if the deadline is missed. c) Additional Announcements SSUET Entry Test Exemption Available! • You are exempt from the SSUET test of the relevant program if you have passed USAT, NEDUET, MUET, NTS, ETEA, MDCAT, or any public sector university test in 2026. Upload your scorecard on to your application portal under the Other Test section.. OR visit the Admissions Office before the deadline to claim exemption. You may still attempt the SSUET test to improve your score; the highest score will be considered. • Test scores contribute to merit but do not guarantee admission. A processing fee is mandatory for all applicants, including those with a test exemption. #Posters Prospectus Prospectus 2025 Prospectus 2023-24 Prospectus 2022-23 Prospectus 2021-22 Prospectus 2020  Admission Test Requirements Engineering & Sciences Programs: For admission in any Engineering Program 60% (SIXTY PERCENT) of the aggregate marks are required. MBA/MS (Weekend/Evening) – Instructions • SSUET/NTS GAT (General) with a minimum 50% score is required before admission. • Candidates must pass an interview conducted by the departmental postgraduate committee. • For MBA, candidates will follow the HEC-prescribed route. PhD (Weekend/Evening) – Instructions • NTS GAT (General) with a minimum 60% score (valid for one year) is required (mandatory). • SSUET GAT Subjective must also be passed with at least 60%. • Candidates must pass an interview conducted by the departmental postgraduate committee. • Upload a Statement of Purpose on the portal and bring a hard copy for the interview. #Posters Admission Requirement Engineering & Sciences Programs MS Programs: Biomedical Engineering Computer Engineering Civil Engineering Electronic Engineering Electrical Engineering Computer Science Software Engineering Climate Change & Environmental Informatics Data Engineering & Information Management Information Security Mathematics MBA MS, MBA Programs Eligibility & Requirements: Education: Sixteen years of schooling or 4-year education after HSSC or equivalent (minimum 124 credit hours), in a relevant discipline from HEC-recognized degree awarding institutes, with a minimum 2.0 CGPA or 6 0% marks (1st Division) The Board of Advanced Studies will determine any deficiency courses required for applicants from a non-relevant discipline applying to Computing Programs after evaluating the BS transcript during the interview. Note: For equivalent studies in relevant disciplines, an HEC verification and equivalence certificate of 16 years of education is mandatory. Test: 1- SSUET/NTS GAT(General) test must be passed with 50% marks, before admission Note: Valid GRE/HAT/NTS General, conducted by testing bodies accredited by HEC with a required passing score is accepted against SSUET GAT. A valid Gat Card is to be uploaded. Interview: The candidate has to appear in an interview that shall be conducted by the departmental Postgraduate Admission Committee. Ph.D. Programs: PhD in Biomedical Engineering PhD in Computer Engineering PhD in Electronic Engineering PhD in Civil Engineering PhD in Mathematics Ph.D. Programs Eligibility & Requirements: Education: 1- HEC-recognized Master’s degree (MS, MPhil, or equivalent) in a relevant discipline with a minimum CGPA of 3.0 out of 4.0 (in the semester system) or First Division (in the annual system), whether such a degree was obtained from Pakistani or foreign universities. 2- If the CGPA/Percentage is not mentioned on the transcript, the candidate must produce equivalent weightage from the parent university. Test: 1- NTS GAT(General) test must be passed with 60% marks with a 1 year validity. 2- In addition GAT Subjective conducted by SSUET must also be passed with a 60% mark before admission. Interview: An interview must be cleared and shall be conducted by the departmental Postgraduate Admission Committee. Statement of Purpose: Applicants are required to submit a statement of purpose covering the following points: a) Title of the potential research proposal b) Clear articulation of the current understanding of the intended field and ideas for potential research c) Explanation of the intended impact of the proposed research d) The prospective candidates shall demonstrate passion and enthusiasm for the area of research Prospectus Prospectus 2025 Prospectus 2023-24 Prospectus 2022-23 Prospectus 2021-22 Prospectus 2020 Test Instructions Eligibility Criteria Chart Fee Structure Archived – Fee Structure 2024 – 25 Archived -Fall 2023 Fee Structure Admission Process Start online Application Submission Apply online at admissions.ssuet.edu.pk. Upload your photograph (as per instructions) and all required documents in the specified format. Deposit Fee and Collect Admit Card Once the application form is completed, a fee challan will be generated. Deposit the fee at any MCB branch or use the online PayPro payment option. After payment verification, the fee status will be updated in the “Progress” tab. Your Admit Card will be available on the application portal one or two days before the interview date. Selected Candidates List Announcement GAT Results & program-wise list of selected candidates will be published on the website for those who qualify both the SSUET-GAT/ GRE/HAT/NTS and the SSUET interview. Policies & Procedures Manual Sir Syed University of Engineering & Technology Title of Policy: UNDERGRADUATE PROGRAMS ADMISSION POLICY (2025-2026) Revision Date (if any): NIL Policy Area: Undergraduate admissions Policy Number: SSUET/P/Acad Approved by (Statutory Body/ Competent Authority): Approval Date: 16th September 2025 Effective Date: July 25 Date of Issue: 30th September 2025 Total Pages: 31 Policy Statement Sir Syed University of Engineering and Technology (SSUET) is dedicated to maintaining the highest academic standards and ensuring fair and transparent admissions. This policy serves as a comprehensive framework for the admission process for the academic year 2025-26 It aligns with the guidelines and regulations set forth by the Higher Education Commission (HEC) and relevant accrediting councils. This policy applies to all undergraduate students seeking admission, and students, faculty, and staff must understand and adhere to these guidelines. Name Designation Ms. Aneela Mansoor Manager Admissions Prepared by: Prof. Dr. Tahir Qadri Convenor Admissions Committee DQEC Dean Faculty of ECE Reviewed by: Dean Faculty of CVA Registrar Approved by : Vice Chancellor ADMISSION POLICY (2025-2026) (Applicable to all Undergraduate Programs offered by SSUET) 1.0 Preamble Sir Syed University of Engineering and Technology is committed to maintaining high academic standards by identifying applicants who are eligible to be considered for admission. This policy is intended to provide a broad framework and a set of principles for determining admissions of SSUET. 2.0 Introduction The Admission Policy is a critical component of the university's prospectus and is annually approved by the SSUET Academic Council (AC) before its formal implementation. This policy pertains to admissions for the Batches 2025-26. SSUET's admission procedures are designed to align with the requirements of HEC and accrediting councils. Admissions are open to all eligible applicants based on merit, regardless of their caste, creed, color, culture, religion, gender, or domicile. However, acceptance of an admission form does not guarantee admission; it is contingent on merit and seat availability. 3.0 Admission Policy Sir Syed University of Engineering & Technology offers admissions in its undergraduate degree programs as given below: - Note: Acceptance of the admission form does not guarantee admission, which is made based on merit and availability of seats. 3.7 Rejection of Application The University has the right to reject any application or cancel/ withdraw the admission of a student. 3.8 Admission Aptitude Test Admission Policy 2025 - 26 (Ver 2.0) 5 of 23 3.8.1 Test Contents a) The Entry Test can be a computer-based, online or paper-based test. The university reserves the right to offer any type of test or change the type of test for admission without any prior notification. Applicants have the opportunity for multiple attempts to enhance their test results, with each attempt incurring a fee of Rs. 1500. b) The test format is based on the chosen group of study (e.g., Pre-Engineering, Pre-Medical, General Science, Commerce, Humanities). The test includes 100 questions with a time limit of 60 minutes, and there is no negative marking. c) Applicants for the Architecture program will be assessed through a special aptitude test, drawing test, and interview conducted by the SSUET Architecture Department. Note: All Candidates who pass the Test as per the set threshold will qualify for program-wise Merit Calculations. 3.8.2 Mode of Test PLAN A: A Computer/paper-based test will be conducted in SSUET. PLAN B: An online test will be conducted through the SSUET admission portal under special conditions, following the necessary approvals. Students may attempt the test from any location after registering according to the prescribed schedule. Note: Marks will be awarded as mentioned below in section 3.10. 3.9 Hafiz-e-Quran Applicants who are Hafiz-e-Quran are eligible for an additional 20 marks in HSC I / Equivalent Examination Marks issued by IBCC for A-Level/ Equivalent examination, subject to the presentation of the original sanad from Wifaq-ul-Madaris Arabia Pakistan. This addition is considered for determining the candidate's merit and does not affect the eligibility criteria for admission. 3.10 Merit Determination for Admission The Admission Committee will process the applications on the basis of merit as determined by the applicant’s previous academic record and his/her performance in the Aptitude Test. This first installment comprises: i) Admission Fee (Non-refundable) ii) Security Deposit (Refundable) iii) Student Activity Fee iv) Semester Registration Fee v) Examination Fee vi) Studio Fee (BAR) Payments can be made through two methods. Students may pay directly at any MCB branch. The bank accepts payments in cash, through a pay order, or via a demand draft in favor of “Sir Syed University of Engineering & Technology, Karachi”. Alternatively, for those who prefer digital transactions, payments can be made online through the university's official Paypro online payment portal. This secure platform allows for easy and efficient payment processing from anywhere with internet access. Students are advised to retain their payment receipts for their records, regardless of the payment method chosen. Note that IBFT payments are strictly not allowed. The examinations are also conducted in English. 3.18 Employment/Simultaneous Enrolment All undergraduate degree programs are regular full-time programs. No student admitted to this University shall be allowed to engage himself/ herself in employment or maintain simultaneous enrollment in any other course of studies in any educational institution. Violation of the above may lead to cancellation of admission. 3.19 Cancellation of Admission/ Enrolment a) In case, at any stage, it is found that the documents based on which admission was granted are forged/tampered / bogus, the admission of the student will be cancelled and the fee paid shall be forfeited. The university also reserves the right to legal action. b) If a student fails to attend classes for four weeks consecutively in a regular semester (two weeks in summer semester), without prior approval, his/her admission may be suspended. However, he/she may be allowed to continue studies in the next semester on the recommendations of the Chairperson/ Dean on the payment of a prescribed fee. c) Admission of any such student of any Year/ Semester who has been suspended/ rusticated from the University on account of a serious breach of discipline for any specified period shall be cancelled and notified. However, after expiry of the period, the student may be allowed readmission in the same Year/Semester with junior batch, if otherwise eligible. d) Admission and enrolment of any such student of any Year/ Semester who has been expelled from the University on account of major breach of discipline shall be cancelled after due process and subsequently notified. The student shall not be eligible for any subsequent admission in the University. Note:- All HEC and respective accreditation council Rules and Regulations are applicable in addition to Sir Syed University of Engineering & Technology Rules & Regulations. 4.0 ADMISSION PROCEDURE 4.1 Submission of Application for Admission 1. The admission test registration and Processing fee for all programs is Rs. 3,900/-. 2. The Candidates have to visit admissions.ssuet.edu.pk and complete the online registration process through his/her email address. Admission Policy 2025 - 26 (Ver 2.0) 11 of 23 3. Fill up the admission form step by step. Also, attach (upload) the required documents (Scanned Copies). 4. Carefully select the preferred choices. Once the form is submitted, the choices cannot be changed. 5. Take a printout of the voucher & submit it in any MCB bank OR use available ONLINE payment options only. Note: IBFT payments are strictly not allowed (for details visit www.ssuet.edu.pk). 6. You must upload the paid voucher receipt on the application portal. 7. Admit cards will be issued a day before the entry test series starts to all candidates on the Admission Portal Dashboard who have completed the form requirements and uploaded the scanned copy of the paid challan on the application portal, once verified by the SSUET Accounts Office. 4.2 Admission Test The test can be a computer-based, online, or paper-based test. The university reserves the right to offer any type of test or change the type of test for admission without any prior notification. Candidate has to attempt (as per schedule and mode of test plan) an Aptitude Test that will comprise MCQ questions to the standard of HSC (Pre-Engineering/ Science General/ Pre-Medical/ Commerce) as per the applied Program. The admission aptitude test result is announced on the SSUET website (www.ssuet.edu.pk). All Candidates who pass the Admission Test as per the set threshold qualify for department-wise Merit Calculations and the selection process. Applicants have the opportunity for multiple attempts to enhance their test results, with each attempt incurring a fee of Rs. 1500. 4.2.1 Drawing Test & Interview Applicant has to attempt (as per schedule and mode of test plan) the Drawing Test & interview that will comprise several sections in case of application for Bachelor of Architecture & Bachelor of Interior Design admission. The drawing test & Interview results have been announced on the SSUET website (www.ssuet.edu.pk). All candidates who pass the drawing test, and interview, as per the set threshold, qualify for the Bachelor of Architecture & Bachelor of Interior Design program merit calculations and selection process. pages.content: Frequently Asked Questions 1. When will the admissions begin? Please refer to our website www.ssuet.edu.pk for updated information. 2. Are campus tours / visits open? Campus tours / visits are open for applicants and their parents during visiting hours i.e. Monday to Friday 9:00 am to 05:00 pm subject to adhering to strict SOPs like mandatory wearing of masks, sanitizers, transparent water bottles etc. 3. Where are you located? ST-16 University Rd, Block 5 Gulshan-e-Iqbal, Karachi, Karachi City, Sindh. 4. Will I be eligible to apply if I am waiting for results or appearing in final year exams? Yes, all those candidates whose Intermediate / A level / Equivalent exams / results are delayed due to the COVID-19 threat are eligible to apply for admissions in Fall 2021 semester at SSUET. 5. What is the process to apply for admissions? The process to apply for admissions is as follows: Step 1: Go to the SSUET’s online application portal Step 2: Register yourself to login to the portal Step 3: Fill out all the sections of the form respectively. Make sure that you have filled all the fields where information is required. Step 4: Upload the documents in required format. Step 5: Save and submit the application. Step 6: Pay the application fee through online mode or manual mode. Once registered, the admit card will be issued before the admission test is scheduled. Note: In case of having trouble while filling the form, email the screenshot of the issue with your Application ID at admissions@ssuet.edu.pk 6. How many undergraduate programs I can apply for? Undergraduate applicants can apply for up to minimum 5 or maximum 10 programs. 7. Is it possible to make changes to the online application after submitting it? No, you cannot make changes to the application once it is submitted. However, you can send a request to Admissions Office on admissions@ssuet.edu.pk for desired changes in your application details. 8. What if I am having trouble submitting my form? To be able to submit your application, every section must be ticked as complete. Please avoid clicking multiple times as this can also cause problems. If it locks your attempts, this will reset automatically after two minutes. 9. What is the last date for submission of forms and for the aptitude test? Please refer to the link https://www.ssuet.edu.pk/ug/ for updated information. 10. What will be the Admission test consist of? Candidate has to attempt an aptitude test that will comprise over the MCQs questions to the standard of HSC (Intermediate Science/commerce) as per applied program.  The Admission Test will consist of minimum five components according to the Chosen program. For Undergraduate Programs Test components will be English, Logical & Reasoning / General Knowledge, Maths/ Business Maths, Physics, (Computer/ Biology / Chemistry / Statistics).  Applicants interested in Architecture programs will be assessed through Drawing test and interview conducted by the university in addition to the aptitude test.  University conducts its own GAT based MS, PhD entry test. However, we also consider GAT-NTS for admission in Postgraduate Programs. 11. What is the duration of the aptitude test? Duration of the Test shall be two to three hours according to the chosen program. 12. When will the result of the aptitude test be announced? Admission aptitude test result is announced on SSUET website www.ssuet.edu.pk . All candidates who pass the test as per the set threshold qualify for Department-wise Merit calculations. 13. What is the eligibility criteria for Engineering and Non-Engineering programs? The minimum eligibility criteria to apply for Engineering Programs is 60% in a relevant discipline of Science as guided by the PEC, while 50% is the minimum percentage required to apply for Non-Engineering Programs with a relevant group of subjects as per the requirement of the chosen degree program. The minimum required percentage to apply in BBA Program is 45%. A full list of our academic programs and their minimum eligibility criteria can be found on our website www.ssuet.edu.pk 14. What is the criteria for foreign students? HEC Foreign Student policy applies to subject students. They are required to attain HEC Equivalence Certificate and other regulatory bodies endorsement as well as endorsement from Foreign Ministry of Pakistan to pursue higher studies in Pakistan. The Fee Structure for Foreign Students is different. 15. What is the criteria for A-level students? A level students are required to provide passing evidence in minimum 3 Principal Subjects with required % of the applied program. Candidates must submit the IBCC Equivalence Certificate of O and A-Level Studies. 16. What is the criteria for Diploma Students in Engineering programs? Candidates holding a 3-year Diploma /DAE (equivalent to Intermediate) in a relevant discipline are eligible for admission in engineering programs against DAE based quota if their scores are equivalent or above 60%. Candidates must submit their IBCC Equivalence Certificate of DAE. 17. How do you determine the merit? The Admissions Committee will process the applications on the basis of merit as determined by the applicant’s previous academic record and his /her performance in the aptitude test. Additional Marks for Hifz-e-Quran is applicable. For further details, please refer to our website www.ssuet.edu.pk 18. Is there any quota? The admissions at SSUET are purely on open merit basis in all degree programs. However, there are DAE quota based seats available in Engineering programs as per the PEC Guidelines. 19. Is there any quota reserved for sports and sponsors? The candidates who are outstanding sportsmen or recommended by any sponsor are eligible for admission under the reserved seats category provided candidates fulfil the eligibility criteria of the applied program. 20. What is the credit transfer policy from other universities? The University will entertain students who wants to transfer at SSUET from any other HEC recognized universities in all discipline subject to availability of seats, moreover, fulfilling all the University’s laid down rules for migration. 21. What does “provisionally accepted” mean? Provisional admissions will be offered to all candidates who qualify as per Merit. Candidates will however be required to provide HSC / Equivalent mark sheet with having minimum marks as per eligibility criteria of the offered program soon after the announcement of their respective results. In case of non-submission or having secured lesser than the eligibility marks, the admission will be cancelled. 22. What is the fee structure of programs offered? Open the link for detailed information: https://www.ssuet.edu.pk/charges/ 23. Does SSUET offer any kind of scholarship or easy payment plans? INTRODUCTION ...................................................................................................................................................... 4 2. INTRODUCTION This policy covers important information about tuition, other fee charges and the circumstances in which students are entitled to receive a refund. Previously, the Higher Education Commission approved and circulated Two (02) fee refund policies in 2012, namely “National Leve Fee Refund Policy (NLFRP), 2012” and National fee refund policy (NFRP) in 2015 respectively. 2. AIMS AND OBJECTIVES 2.1. The purpose of the policy is to set out clearly the conditions on which refunds of such fee may be made, the amount, the applicable dates, any deduction made from the refund and the process by which withdrawals from programs are officially recorded. 2.2. A student who withdraws from a semester/course(s) completely or is otherwise withdrawn or de- enrolled by a university is subject to a Fee Refund as per this policy. 2.3. The purpose of this policy is to provide guidance on when refunds of fee will be made by a university when a student(s) withdraws, or a program is withdrawn and how refunds will be calculated. This relates to the portion of the fee that is paid directly by the student his/her guardian or by a private sponsor and covers full undergraduate and postgraduate programs. 2.4. To ensure that HEIs contribute to the betterment of students, this policy has been made pursuant to the powers granted to the HEC under the Higher Education Commission Ordinance, 2002. The implementation of this policy is binding on all HEIs in the country, whether operating in the public or private sectors. Violation(s) or failure(s) to comply with the HEC’s policies may lead to regulatory action by HEC against that non- compliant HEI(s). 3. SCOPE 3.1. This policy applies to all categories and levels of Pakistani students enrolled in a higher education undergraduate and graduate degree program in Public and Private Sector Institutions including affiliated colleges in Pakistan. 4 | P a g e 4. CANCELLATION/WITHDRAWAL 4.1. Students canceling or withdrawing from a program of study may be entitled to a refund of Tuition Fee. Generally, those students will qualify for a refund whose request for a fee refund falls under one of the categories: i. Personal Emergencies. ii. Health Reasons, iii. Care of and medical reasons for Family Members. iv. Legal/Immigration Matters. v. Delay in admission in other Universities. vi. Other (these reasons will be considered on an individual case basis). 4.2. If a student is required to leave the program due to non-fulfillment of entry/admission requirements upon official announcement of examination results, he/she will be eligible for a refund. 5. POSTPONEMENT 5.1. The Tuition Fee can be carried forward and utilized for the following subsequent semester if a student seeks postponement of his/her studies within Two (2) weeks of the commencement of the semester. 5.2. However, after the above-mentioned time frame, any request for the Tuition Fee to be carried forward shall only be permitted on medical grounds, duly verified by a medical officer of the University or by a Doctor of a Government Hospital. The HEI, however, may inquire about the authenticity/validity of the medical certificate/advice of the doctor. 6. REFUNDABLE FEE 7. Tuition Fee: 7.1. Application for a refund of Fee can be made by completing the appropriate form and submitting the proof of payment. Any refund will be paid to the student or his/her parents/guardians/ sponsoring body. 5 | P a g e 7.2. The refund amount of Tuition Fee is subject to the following schedule: Timeline Percentage of Fee Upto 10th day of commencement of classes 100% fee refund Upto 15th day of commencement of classes 80% fee refund Upto 20th day of commencement of classes 60% fee refund Upto 30th day of commencement of classes 50 % fee refund 31st day onwards of commencement of classes No Refund Note: The timelines for refund of tuition fee are inclusive of the weekends. 8. Laboratory Fee: The Laboratory fee contains the following types: a. Computer Laboratory: Compulsory for all students b. Science Laboratory: Compulsory for all students who enroll in one or more science subjects such as Biology, Chemistry, Physics etc. c. Engineering Laboratory: Compulsory for all engineering students. d. Medical Laboratory: Compulsory for Medical and Health Sciences students. e. Other Laboratory: Compulsory for students f. The laboratory fee is 100% refundable minus (-) the days a student has availed of that facility(es). 9. Library Fee: 9.1. The library/digital library fee is completely refundable. 10. Transport Fee: 10.1. The fee submitted for transportation is completely refundable. 10.2. The transport fee is 100% refundable minus (-) the days a student has availed of that facility(es). 11. Utilities Fee: 11.1. The fee submitted for utilities/services is completely refundable. 11.2. The Utilities fee is 100% refundable minus (-) the days a student has availed of that facility(es). 12. Security/Deposit Fee: 12.1. Payable by all new students together with the first-semester tuition fee, this fee is refundable after deductions are made for the damage/loss (if any) caused by the student. 12.2. The deposit is fully refundable after the student has completed his/her duration of 6 | P a g e studies or has withdrawn/transferred to another university. 13. Examination Fee: 13.1. The fee submitted as an examination fee is completely refundable. 14. Fee for Curricular/Co-Curricular Activities: 14.1. The fee submitted for curricular, co-curricular, extra-curricular, sports, tours, field trips etc. activities is completely refundable. The Curricular/co-curricular, extra-curricular, fee is 100% refundable minus (-) the days a student has availed of that activity(es). 15. Fee Transfer: 15.1. A student who transfers to another program within the university will be eligible for fee transfer to the new program. If there’s difference of fee in between the two programs of that university than: a. In case the fee difference is Positive then the difference will be paid by the student. b. In case the fee difference is negative then the difference will be paid to the student. 16. NON-REFUNDABLE FEE 17. Admission Fee: 17.1. The fee paid as an admission fee is nonrefundable. 17.2. However, it may be noted that in case, a student paid admission fee in one of the constituents/affiliated colleges of the university, and he/she/transgender is also offered admission in another college in the same program, then the admission fee paid to the earlier college is to be transferred to the later college in respect of that student. 18. Registration/Application Fee: 18.1. Any Fee, payable at the time of initial application is non-refundable under any circumstances. 19. No Refund: 19.1. A student expelled from the university due to disciplinary misconduct, shall not be eligible for any refund, except for the refundable Security/Deposit Fee. 7 | P a g e

pages.content: Policies & Procedures Manual Sir Syed University of Engineering & Technology Title of Policy: RULES AND REGULATIONS FOR THE DEGREE OF PhD Revision Date (if any): 05-03-2024 Policy Area: PG Programs Policy Number: SSUET/P/Acad/008-V8 Approved by (Statutory Body): 57th AC and 43rd BASR Approval Date: 24-04-2024 Effective Date: 05-03-2024 Date of Issue: 24-04-2024 Total Pages: 10 Policy Statement It is the policy of SSUET to establish a quality management system that meets the quality standards expected by our stakeholders. To achieve this, SSUET management is committed to continuous improvement in all areas of activities. Name Designation Date Prepared by: Prof. Dr. Muhammad Tahir Qadri Director PGS Prof. Dr. Mir Shabbar Ali Dean FoCV&AR Prof. Dr. Muhammad Aamir Dean FoECE 05-03-2024 Prof. Dr. Muhammad Asif Dean FoCO&AS Dr. Muhammad Rehan Director QEC Board of Advanced Studies and Research (BASR) Reviewed by: 24-04-2024 RULES AND REGULATIONS FOR THE DEGREE OF DOCTOR OF PHILOSOPHY (PhD) 1.0 Preamble Rules and regulations are formulated for the postgraduate studies leading to the Degree of Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) at Sir Syed University of Engineering and Technology, Karachi and are updated when required. These rules and regulations are updated in accordance with the HEC’s Graduate Education Policy – 2023, shared via notification # 15-54/Coord/2019/HEC/(QAD)/560 dated 10th July 2023. 2.0 Applicability These PhD Rules (version 8) are applicable to all PhD Scholars admitted in Spring 2024 Session and Onwards, whereas for previous Batches, PhD Rules (Version 7) is applicable. 3.0 Admission Requirements 3.1 Education: HEC recognized Master’s degree (MS, MPhil or equivalent) in relevant discipline with minimum CGPA of 3.0 out of 4.0 (in the semester system) or First Division (in the annual system), whether such degree was obtained from Pakistani or foreign universities. 3.2 If the CGPA/Percentage is not mentioned on the transcript, the candidate must produce equivalent weightage from the parent university. 3.3 Test: A GAT-General Test conducted by National Testing Service (NTS), passed with minimum 60% marks. In addition to that a GAT-Subject test conducted by SSUET MUST be passed with minimum 60% marks. 3.4 Interview: An interview must be cleared that shall be conducted by the departmental Postgraduate Admission Committee. 3.5 Statement of Purpose: Applicants are required to submit a Statement of Purpose covering following points, i. Title of the potential research proposal ii. Clear articulation of the current understanding of the intended field and ideas for potential research iii. Explanation of the intended impact of the proposed research iv. The prospective candidates shall demonstrate passion and enthusiasm for the area of research. 4.0 Admission Procedure 4.1 Students seeking admission in the PhD programme shall submit their application to the Admissions Office, though prescribed application form along with relevant documents and Statement of Purpose. 4.2 The Admissions Office shall conduct the Admissions Test as prescribed in section 3.3. 4.3 A departmental PhD admission committee, comprising of at least 2 senior PhD faculty members and one external member, shall be proposed by the chairperson of the department and approved by the Vice Chancellor. 4.4 The departmental Postgraduate Admission Committee shall conduct the interview and assess an applicant’s suitability while considering the following: 4.4.1 The admission requirements described in para 3.0. 4.4.2 The availability of potential PhD supervisors and the maximum number of PhD students that can be admitted in a programme in light of HEC’s policy on the subject. 4.4.3 The availability of requisite resources, in light of the candidate’s statement of purpose, to train and supervise the doctoral candidate in the subspecialty in which the applicant is interested. 4.4.4 Prerequisite courses that an applicant may need in order to meet a program’s requirements. 4.5 The departmental Postgraduate Admission Committee, with the consent of the candidate, will also recommend a supervisor (and a co-supervisor if required) for each candidate recommended for admission in accordance with para 6.0. 4.6 The departmental Postgraduate Admission Committee shall forward its recommendations to the PGP office through the Chairperson of the department. 4.7 The recommendations of the relevant Postgraduate Admission Committee shall be forwarded to the Admissions Office for necessary approvals and announcement of results to the applicants. 5.0 Scheme of Implementation 5.1 Admission: Initially provisional admission shall be given. 5.2 Duration: The duration for completing the PhD degree requirements shall be minimum 03 years and maximum 08 years from the date of enrolment. 5.3 Coursework: 5.3.1 Course work of minimum 18 credit hours (06 PhD level courses) is required to be completed within 1st three semesters of initial enrollment. These 18 credit hours will be in addition to any pre-requisite courses recommended by the supervisor, GC. 5.3.2 The courses shall be offered through regular classes (i.e., classes taught on campus by full-time faculty members of the university) 5.3.2 A student enrolled in a PhD programme may take up to 06 credit hours of PhD level courses from other disciplines subject to approval of individual courses as being acceptable by the department towards the student’s PhD degree. 5.3.2 (a) None of the PhD student is allowed to take any PhD Course towards his/her PhD course work which he/she has already taken in Masters Level or at least with 70% similar contents of that course which they have already taken. 5.3.2 (b) If there is a similar course, the student will submit the request to Concerned Dean through course teacher, to determine the similarity of both course along with their course contents. 5.3.2 (c) It will be the sole responsibility of the PhD student to comply 5.3.2 (a) rule and verify their Masters Level Courses. 5.3.2 (d) At any point of time, the Examination department has the right to cancel that course towards his/her PhD course work in case of non-compliance. 5.3.3 Minimum CGPA is required to be 3.0 out of 4.0 in the 18 credit hours of PhD level courses that are to be counted towards PhD coursework. 5.3.4 A student may repeat a PhD level course in which grade point of less than 3.0 is achieved to improve the CGPA. Improvement is allowed only once for a course. The better grade will be used in the computation of CGPA. 5.3.5 If an elective course cannot be offered for repetition due to unavoidable circumstances, a student may take an alternative elective course with the approval of Supervisor and shall get the earned grades. The better grade will be used in the computation of CGPA. 5.4 Comprehensive Examination: A Comprehensive Examination is required to be passed after completing PhD level courses with minimum CGPA of 3.0 and within 1st four Semesters of initial enrollment. The Comprehensive Examination is composed of a written exam. The details of the Comprehensive Examination are given in para 8.0. 5.5 PhD Candidacy: After clearing the Comprehensive Examination, the PhD Candidacy will be awarded after the approval of BASR. 5.6 Research Proposal: 5.6.1 The required coursework, comprehensive exam, and defense of synopsis/research proposals should be completed within the 1st PhD six semesters of the registrations into program. In case of noncompliance, the registration shall be cancelled and transcripts for completion of coursework may be issued to the student. 5.6.2 In an event of force majeure i.e., noncompliance on account of circumstances beyond the control of student, the university may consider the matter in accordance with the procedure laid by HEC. 5.6.3 After obtaining the PhD candidacy, the student is required to submit the written research proposal in consultation with Guidance Committee (GC) and present it in a seminar. 5.6.4 After having successfully defended the research proposal, the proposal shall be recommended by the GC for approval from BASR. 5.6.5 The proposal should identify the research problem, review the relevant literature, describe the tasks planned to solve the problem, and propose a timeline for the completion of the research work. 5.6.6 Additionally, they are required to demonstrate how their proposed solution offers a novel approach to addressing this problem. Instead of using the existing techniques with slight modifications, the candidate is required to introduce a genuinely new methodologies aimed to solve the identified problem. 5.6.7 The research area of the PhD researcher shall also correspond to the community needs at regional and local levels and comply with the priority national research agenda and also Signify emerging areas of research that coincide preferably with sustainable development goals (SDGs) 5.6.8 If the student’s GC deems that the proposal needs further work, it may apprise the candidate appropriately, assigning a timeline for a proposal re-defense. 5.7 Research Work: During PhD candidacy, the scholar shall engage in creative and innovative research work (equivalent to 30 credit hours) leading to an original PhD thesis. The research work must include novel methodologies rather than using already existing algorithms by just changing their parameters. 5.8 Review of Progress: 5.8.1 The progress of a PhD student shall be reviewed biannually during the period of research. 5.8.1.1 Minor Review of Progress: The minor review of progress shall be undertaken in Spring Semester. The PhD student shall submit the prescribed progress review form to GC. The committee shall review the progress and inform the BASR about the progress along with any recommendations if required. 5.8.1.2 Major Review of Progress: The major review of progress shall be undertaken in Fall Semester. As a part of this review, the PhD student shall deliver an open seminar on his/her research work and complete the prescribed progress review form. The GC shall review the progress considering the seminar and the progress report, and inform the BASR about the progress along with any recommendations if required. 5.8.2 Failing to submit two consecutive progress reports or failing to demonstrate satisfactory performance in two consecutive progress reviews may result in expulsion from the PhD programme on approval of BASR. 5.9 Publications: 5.9.1 For award of PhD degree, a PhD researcher shall be required to publish research articles meeting the following criteria: At least: 5.9.3.1 One research article in W category journal (As categorized in HJRS at the time of acceptance of the research article) or two research articles in X category journals, for Science disciplines 5.9.3.2 One research article in X category journal or two research articles in Y category journals, for Social Science disciplines 5.9.2 The PhD researcher shall be the first author of these publications. 5.9.3 The research article shall be relevant to the PhD research work of the PhD researcher. 5.9.4 The article shall be published after approval of the research synopsis. 5.9.5 The article shall be published in a relevant research journal. 5.10 Thesis Examination and Defence: The student after completing the research work shall document research details in a PhD thesis and submit it for examination and subsequent defence. The details of thesis examination and defence are given in section Para 9.0 respectively. 5.11 Leave of Absence: 5.11.1 A candidate, who is temporarily unable to continue research because of unavoidable circumstances, should file an application to the BASR through the supervisor for leave of absence. Such leaves of absence shall not exceed twelve months in total. Such leaves will be subject to approval from BASR. 5.11.2 This leave of absence does not extend the degree duration requirements defined in Para 5.2. 5.11.3 When the candidate returns from the leave, the Postgraduate Programme Office (PGP) on the recommendations of Supervisor may allow the student to continue and to inform BASR 5.12 Changes: A supervisor, GC member or research topic may be changed with considerable justification, subject to BASR approval. 6.0 PhD Supervisor 6.1. Criteria to Be a PhD Supervisor To be a PhD Supervisor, a faculty member shall meet the following requirements and submit the PhD Supervisor Approval Form, for the approval from BASR. 6.1.1 General Requirements for PhD Supervisor: a) A PhD degree from a HEC-accredited national/international university. b) A regular/adjunct faculty member of the University, whereas a co-supervisor can be selected from outside the university. c) The topic must be related to the student's research area and there should be NO CONFLICT OF INTEREST in personnel, financial or professional stakes. d) A PhD Supervisor can supervise not more than five PhD students simultaneously. Furthermore, fresh PhDs can supervise MS/MPhil and co-supervise PhD students, while a PhD faculty member, after two years of obtaining (date of issuance) of PhD Degree, can supervise one PhD student in the third year, two PhD students in the fourth year, and maximum up to five PhD students in the fifth year and onwards, subject to the other conditions outlined in this policy. e) Fulfilling the Publication Requirements as per section 6.2.2 of this policy. f) Final approval for the PhD Supervisor will be obtained from the BASR. ** All the previously HEC approved PhD Supervisors shall remain approved until the date mentioned on their award letter, issued by HEC 6.2.2 Publication Requirements for PhD Supervisor: In addition to fulfilling the General Requirements, a PhD supervisor must publish research articles in the HEC’s recognized research journals and the category specified in the HJRS for the publication year. These conditions are different for different disciplines and aim to ensure that the potential PhD supervisor is an active researcher: A. Specific Requirements for Science and Technology: For indigenous and foreign PhDs: i. Within the last 3 years after PhD: at least one research publications in W category journal. OR ii. Within last 5 years after PhD: at least five research publications in X category journal. B. Specific Requirements for Social Science, Arts and Humanities and Business Education: For indigenous and foreign PhDs: i. Within the last 3 years after PhD: at least one research publication in W category journal. OR ii. Within the last 5 years after PhD: at least five research publications in X and Y category journal. C. Specific Requirements for Regional and National Languages: For indigenous and foreign PhDs: i. Within the last 3 years after PhD: at least one research publication in X category journal. OR ii. Within the last 5 years after PhD: at least five research publications in X or Y category journal. 6.2.3 Procedure to Apply for PhD Supervisor A PhD Faculty member, who intends to be a PhD Supervisor, is required to submit the “PhD Supervisor” form along with all documents, in PGP Office through Concerned Chairperson, atleast 2 weeks before the BASR. 7.0 Guidance Committee (GC) 7.1 A Doctoral GC should be formed at the earliest after the admission of a student into the PhD program. The GC must be formed before the Comprehensive Examination of the student. 7.2 The GC shall comprise of PhD qualified members. The GC shall be composed of at least three members including the supervisor, the co-supervisor (if appointed), at least one internal expert and at least one external expert from a reputed university, R&D organization or relevant industry. The student's supervisor shall chair the GC meetings. 7.3 The chairperson of the department in consultation with the student and the supervisor shall propose GC members. The committee shall be approved by BASR. 7.4 The GC shall hold its meetings at least once a year. 8.0 Comprehensive Examination 8.1 The comprehensive examination is required to be passed after completing PhD level courses with minimum CGPA of 3.0 and within 1st four Semesters of initial enrolment. In case of noncompliance, the registration shall be cancelled and transcript for completion of coursework may be issued to the student 8.2 The Comprehensive Examination shall comprise of written examination focusing on the knowledge covered in the entire PhD coursework. 8.3 The chairperson of the concerned department shall supervise the Written Exam including allocation of examiners, preparation of question papers and conduction of the examination. In case the department’s chairperson is also the student’s supervisor, the Dean or his nominee shall supervise the examination. 8.4 The examination shall be composed of 01 composite question paper with 06 sections (one for each course from PhD coursework) with no choice in questions to be answered. Maximum allowed time shall be 30 minutes for each section. 8.5 Minimum passing marks are 60% in aggregate, expressed in terms of Pass/Fail. 8.6 A student is allowed to appear for Comprehensive Exam maximum two times. 9.0 PhD Final Thesis Dissertation 9.1 Doctoral Dissertation Each PhD researcher shall write a doctoral dissertation reflecting relevance, credibility, effectiveness and legitimacy of the research. The dissertation must be an original and innovative contribution to knowledge that contributes to solving socioeconomic problems. Following guidelines must be observed for the doctoral dissertation. 9.1.1 Quality in Reporting The quality of presentation and reporting in dissertation shall reflect the following characteristics: 9.1.1.1 The document is well written. 9.1.1.2 The contents are balanced, well organized, appropriately styled; clearly structured, and well cohered; and 9.1.1.3 The document is free from grammatical and spelling errors and flawed terminology. 9.1.1.4 Minor shortcomings such as inaccurate use of acronyms and clumsy looking sentence structure have been addressed. 9.1.2 Methodological Quality The following guidelines shall be useful in making the PhD Research methodologically sound. A. Guidelines ensuring the quality of QUALITATIVE Research: A PhD research dissertation, based on the Qualitative Research methods should satisfy, at least, the following questions: a. “Does the research, as reported, illuminate the subjective meaning, actions and contexts of those being researched?” b. “Is there evidence of the adaption and responsiveness of the research design to the circumstances and issues of real-life social settings met during the course of the study?” c. “Does the sample produce the type of knowledge necessary to understand the structures and processes within which the individuals or situations are located?” d. “Is the description provided detailed enough to allow the researcher or reader to interpret the meaning and context of what is being researched?’ e. “How are the different sources of knowledge about the same issue compared and contrasted?” f. “Are subjective perceptions and experiences treated as knowledge in their own right?” g. “How does the research move from a description of the data through quotation or examples to an analysis and interpretation of the meaning and significance of it?” B. Guidelines ensuring the quality of QUANTITATIVE Research: a. Reliability – are the results repeatable? b. Validity – does it measure what it says? c. Internal validity – do the research results indicate what they appear to be? d. External validity – can the results be generalized to other settings (ecological validity) and to other populations (population validity? e. Replicability – are the results of the study reproducible 9.1.3 Appropriateness of the Methods to the Aims of the Study To achieve the research objectives, the alignment of the research approach and methods is necessary. Therefore, a PhD dissertation, at least, shall: a. Reflect a fair proportion of latest knowledge of contemporary techniques and methods in relation to study objectives. b. Contain detailed and easily comprehensible discussions regarding the applied methods and techniques. c. Justify the use of methods and techniques to achieve study objectives. d. Show evaluation of obtained results in relation with study objectives. And: e. The methods and techniques used should justify the results obtained. f. The obtained results should support the study objectives. 9.1.4 Relevance to the Policy and Practice The research should have significantly answered questions related to policy and practice in that area, establishing its usefulness and usability. Accordingly, a PhD dissertation, at least, shall: a. Reflect judicious evaluation of study results in relation with policy related aims and goals undertaken while starting the research. b. Discuss the practical implications of the study results in association with the developing practices in that area. c. Establish usefulness of the study results for devising policy as stated in the beginning. d. Discuss how the resulting policy would be useful for the organization/society. And: e. The study output should be significant enough to be published or patented. f. The assessment of the results performed by the author must not be superficial and lacking substance. 9.2 PhD Thesis Submission 9.2.1 On the recommendation of the supervisor, the thesis shall be first given to GC for internal evaluation. If GC approves that the thesis is of a quality suitable for doctoral thesis, then the thesis should be submitted to PGP office for further examination. 9.2.2 A candidate may submit the thesis for evaluation only after the following conditions are met: i. Acceptance of research articles as per para 5.9. ii. Completion of minimum 02 years in PhD candidacy. iii. Clearance of dues. iv. Satisfactory plagiarism report from supervisor. v. Recommendation of GC for external evaluation. vi. Fulfilling any other conditions laid down by HEC or University. 9.2.3 Four soft-bound copies and one electronic copy of the thesis shall be submitted to the PGP office with the recommendation of the GC, Concerned Chairperson and Concerned Dean through QEC Department. 9.3 External Evaluation of PhD Dissertation The PhD dissertation must be evaluated by: a. At least two external experts who shall be either: i. PhD faculty member from the world top 500 universities ranked by the Times Higher Education or QS World Ranking in the year corresponding to dissertation evaluation year OR ii. Pakistan-based Distinguished National Professors, Meritorious Professors from any national university; Professors from top universities ranked by HEC; Professors from any Pakistani University having a minimum H-Index 30 for Sciences, 15 for Social Sciences or 8 for Art & Humanities as determined by Web of Science. OR b. At least one external expert qualifying any one of the conditions mentioned at ‘a’ above if the PhD candidate publishes dissertation research in a peer-reviewed journal that is classified by the HEC in category W for Sciences and X or above for Social Sciences. 9.4 Gui delines for Selection of External Evaluators 9.4.1 The following general guidelines shall, at least, be observed while selecting external evaluator: i. Relevance of Expertise: in the same or related fields as in the dissertation. ii. No Conflict of Interest: in personal, financial, or professional stakes in a particular decision or outcome. iii. Objectivity: capable of making unbiased evaluations. iv. Diversity: in terms of geography, culture, professional backgrounds etc. v. Reputation: must be good in the field, with a track record of fair and thorough evaluations. vi. Availability: should have the time and availability to review the dissertation. vii. Professionalism: capable of conducting themselves in a professional and respectful manner throughout the evaluation and defense process (if applicable). viii. Communication: capable of providing clear and constructive feedback on the dissertation. ix. Confidentiality: capable of maintaining confidentiality and protecting the intellectual property of the dissertation. x. Compatibility: well-versed with the research methodology, approach, and theories used in the dissertation. 9.4.2 The Vice Chancellor shall appoint the external foreign evaluators considering the list of names suggested by the supervisor. The supervisor shall suggest at least five names of potential foreign evaluators, considering the following parameters: Relevancy, No Conflict of Interest, Objectivity, Diversity, Reputation, Availability, Professionalism, Communication, Confidentiality, Compatibility. 9.4.3 Evaluation report by the evaluator(s) (as per section 9.3) has to be positive before the student can be asked to carry out final defense. 9.5 Thesis Open Defense 9.5.1 An open defense of the dissertation is required after positive evaluation of the dissertation. In general, the following minimum principles and guidelines shall be ensured: i. Public Announcement: On the university website and other forums of communication, so that anyone interested can participate. ii. Public Access: Within or outside the university such as community/town halls or important public venues. iii. Neutral Chair: To ensure that defense was conducted fairly and in accordance with the rules and regulations. iv. Review Committee: To evaluate the dissertation and defense. v. Presentation: of the dissertation by the PhD researcher vi. Question and Answer Session: To provide a basis for defense evaluation. vii. Objective Evaluation: based on the quality of the research and the researcher’s ability to defend. 9.5.2 The Vice Chancellor shall appoint the PhD Defense Committee to conduct open defense. The committee shall be composed of the following members: 1. Concerned Dean or Chairperson of the department 2. One Internal Examiner 3. One External Examiner 9.5.1 The student shall give the seminar which will be open to all including invitees followed by close examination by the Defense Committee. 9.5.2 The Defense Committee shall express the FINAL Decision in the following terms: • Pass or • Pass with minor amendments or • Deferred for resubmission and re-defense or. • Fail (in exceptional circumstances and for the reasons to be recorded by the defense committee) 9.5.4 The Defense Committee shall inform its decision to the PGP office which will forward it to BASR for approval. 9.5.5 The final version of the thesis shall be checked for plagiarism by PGP Office, according to HEC Guidelines. 10 Plagiarism and Similarity Test 10.1 Under no circumstances shall a dissertation based on plagiarized research be acceptable. It is the primary responsibility of both PhD researchers and their supervisors to prevent plagiarism. To avoid plagiarism, it is important to follow the provisions outlined in this document i.e., Governing Research Supervision and Research Ethics. 10.2 If a PhD dissertation is found to be plagiarized, it will be handled in accordance with the Anti- Plagiarism Policy issued by the Higher Education Commission, Pakistan, as updated from time to time. 10.3 A similarity test in accordance with the HEC’s Anti-Plagiarism Policy, must be conducted on the dissertation before its submission to the external experts by the student. 10.4 Further details on “Guidelines to Ensure Academic Research Integrity”, “Guidelines on ethics of Using Similarity Detection Software for Administrators”, “Guidelines on ethics of Using Similarity Detection Software for Instructors” and “Guidelines on Interpreting Originality Reports” are available in “SSUET Plagiarism and Similarity Test Policy”. 11 Managing the Grievances of Graduate Students Complete details on managing Grievances of Graduate Students are available in “SSUET Grievances Policy” 12 Withdrawal / Drop from PhD program A student shall be withdrawn / dropped from the PhD degree programme under following conditions: 12.1 Does not register in any semester within one year of obtaining provisional admission. 12.2 Does not register for two consecutive semesters without informing and without approval of BASR. 12.3 CGPA remains below 3.0 on completion of coursework even after availing the chances for improvement of grades. 12.4 Fails to complete coursework requirements within maximum allowed time. 12.5 Fails twice in Part A or Part B of the Comprehensive Examination. 12.6 Fails to complete PhD degree requirements within maximum allowed time. 12.7 On consistent unsatisfactory academic performance when recommended by the GC, and approved by the BASR. 12.8 On disciplinary grounds when recommended by the respective Discipline Committee. 12.9 A student can seek withdrawal from PhD programme at any stage of candidature by requesting BASR through PGP office. 13 Violation of HEC Rules Section 7.3 of HEC's letter no. 15-54/Coord/2019/HEC/(QAD)/560 dated 10th July 2023, is attached as Annex 'A' for reference and compliance by all concerned. The Annex may be amended/replaced when and if HEC revises its policy.

To achieve this, SSUET management is committed to continuous improvement in all areas of activities. Name Designation Date Prepared by: Prof. Dr. Muhammad Tahir Qadri Director PGS Prof. Dr. Mir Shabbar Ali Dean FoCV&AR 05-03-2024 Prof. Dr. Muhammad Aamir Dean FoECE Prof. Dr. Muhammad Asif Dean FoCO&AS Dr. Muhammad Rehan Director QEC Reviewed by: Board of Advanced Studies and Research (BASR) 24-04-2024 Rules and Regulations for the Degree of Master of Science (MS) RULES AND REGULATIONS FOR THE DEGREE OF MASTER OF SCIENCE (MS) 1.0 Preamble Rules and regulations are formulated for the postgraduate studies leading to the Degree of Master of Science (MS) at Sir Syed University of Engineering and Technology, Karachi and are updated when required. These rules and regulations are updated in accordance with the HEC’s Graduate Education Policy – 2023, shared via notification # 15-54/Coord/2019/HEC/(QAD)/560 dated 10th July 2023. 2.0 Applicability These rules are applicable to the students admitted in the Master of Science (MS) programme of SSUET with immediate effect including the students who are currently enrolled in Spring 2024 Semester and onwards. 3.0 Admission Requirements 3.1 Education: Sixteen years of schooling or 4-year education after HSSC or equivalent (minimum 124 credit hours), in relevant area from HEC recognized degree awarding institutes, with minimum 2.0 CGPA (in the semester system) st or 60% marks (1 Division, in annual system). 3.2 Test: SSUET GAT(General) / HAT (General)/ NTS (General) test must be passed with 50% marks, prior to the admission in the MS Program. 3.3 Interview: Candidate has to appear in the interview, to be conducted by the departmental Postgraduate Admission Committee. 4.0 Admission Procedure 4.1 Students seeking admission in the MS programme shall submit their application though prescribed application form along with relevant documents. 4.2 A departmental Postgraduate Admission Committee, comprising of at least 02 senior PhD faculty members, shall be proposed by the chairperson of the department and approved by the Dean. 4.3 The departmental Postgraduate Admission Committee shall assess an applicant’s suitability while considering the following: 4.3.1 The admission requirements described in para 3.0. 4.3.2 The maximum number of students that can be admitted in a programme in light of HEC’s policy on the subject. 4.3.3 Prerequisite courses that an applicant may need in order to meet a program’s requirements. 4.4 The departmental Postgraduate Admission Committee shall forward its recommendations to the PGP office through the chairperson of the department. 4.5 The Admission Office, on recommendation of the relevant postgraduate admission committee, shall inform the applicants about the result of their application. 5.0 Scheme of Implementation 5.1 Duration: The duration for completing the MS degree requirements shall be minimum 1.5 years and maximum 04 years from the date of beginning of the first semester in which a student registers for coursework. Page 2 of 3 Rules and Regulations for the Degree of Master of Science (MS) 5.2 Studies: 5.2.1 Minimum 30 credit hours are required to be completed within allowed duration. These 30 credit hours will be in addition to any pre-requisite courses recommended by the departmental Postgraduate Admission Committee. 5.2.2 A student must register in each semester (within the prescribed period) until the completion of degree requirements. Failure to register in two consecutive semesters without prior intimation and approval may result in cancellation of admission without notice. 5.2.3 A student can register in maximum of 04 courses in a semester. 5.2.4 A student enrolled in a MS programme may take up to 09 credit hours of MS level courses from other disciplines subject to approval of individual course(s) as being acceptable by the department towards the student’s MS degree. 5.2.5 A student may undertake MS Thesis of 06 credit hours to be counted towards the 30 credit hours required for the MS degree. The details of MS Thesis are given in para 6.0. 5.2.6 Minimum CGPA is required to be 2.5 out of 4.0 in the MS level courses. 5.2.7 A student may repeat a MS level course in which grade point of less than 2.5 is achieved to improve the CGPA. The better grade will be used in the computation of CGPA. 5.2.8 If an elective course cannot be offered for repetition due to unavoidable circumstances, a student may take an alternative elective course with the approval of the department’s chairperson and shall get the earned grades. The better grade will be used in the computation of CGPA. 6.0 MS Thesis 6.1 A student can register for MS Thesis after completing five courses (15 credit hours). MS Thesis is compulsory for SSUET Faculty members. 6.2 Research Synopsis and Title Defense: 6.2.1 If a student opts to undertake MS Thesis, the student is expected to prepare a Research Synopsis under the guidance of the proposed Supervisor. The concerned Chairman shall form a 3 members committee comparing of proposed Supervisor, Chairperson concerned and one internal member. The student has to defend the Thesis Title in front of this committee. The approval of BASR must be sought for Research Synopsis, Thesis Supervisor and Title Defense, on the recommendations of the committee. 6.2.2 The Research Synopsis/Thesis Topic can be changed on the request of MS student with considerable justification, subject to the approval of BASR. 6.3 Supervi sor: 6.3.1 A person having MS/MPhil or equivalent qualification, meeting HEC’s requirements for experience and having research expertise in the relevant field, can be appointed as a supervisor for an MS Thesis. 6.3.2 The supervisor for MS Thesis shall be selected from the university. Page 3 of 3 Rules and Regulations for the Degree of Master of Science (MS) However, a co-supervisor can be selected from outside the university. Approval of supervisor and co-supervisor must be obtained from BASR. 6.3.3 A supervisor or co-supervisor of a student can be changed on the request of either supervisor or MS student with considerable justification, subject to the approval of BASR. 6.4 Thesis Evaluation: 6.4.1 The student after completing the research work shall document research details in a MS thesis. If the supervisor approves that the thesis is of a quality suitable for MS thesis, then the thesis should be submitted to PGP office for evaluation. 6.4.2 The thesis shall be checked by Supervisor for plagiarism before submitting the thesis for examination. The Editor SSURJ should check the final version of thesis for plagiarism according to HEC Plagiarism Guidelines 6.4.3 The thesis shall be evaluated by the MS Thesis Defence Committee. 6.4.4 The MS Thesis Defence Committee shall be proposed by the chairperson of the department and approved by the Vice Chancellor to conduct open defense. The committee shall be composed of the following members: 1. Supervisor 2. Internal Evaluator 3. External Evaluator The Director PGP or his nominee, if not already a member of the committee, shall attend the Thesis Defence as observer. 6.4.5 The student shall give the seminar which will be open to all. 6.4.6 The Defence Committee shall inform its decision to the PGP office which will be forwarded to the examination department after the approval from BASR, for notification. 7.0 Withdrawal / Drop from MS program A student shall be withdrawn / Dropped from the MS degree programme under following conditions: 7.1 Does not register in any semester within one year of obtaining admission. 7.2 Does not register for two consecutive semesters without informing and without approval of BASR. 7.3 Fails to complete MS degree requirements within maximum allowed time. 7.4 On disciplinary grounds when recommended by the respective Discipline Committee. 7.5 A student can seek withdrawal from MS programme at any stage of candidature by requesting BASR through PGP office. pages.content: Sir Syed University of Engineering & Technology (SSUET) undergraduate fee structure for Fall 2026 - Spring 2027. All fees are subject to annual revision. Self-Finance Admission Fee Policy: at admission, pay the full 1st semester fee plus PKR 250,000 (plus applicable taxes), via cash or pay order in favor of Sir Syed University of Engineering & Technology. A 5% withholding tax applies if the total fee paid during the year exceeds PKR 200,000. Refunds are processed in accordance with the HEC Refund Policy available on the SSUET website. Semester Freeze Policy (applicable from the 2nd semester onward): a semester can be frozen within 15 days of class start by paying the semester registration fee; if the student fails to freeze or register, the status is marked suspended, and reactivation requires paying the semester registration fee for each missed semester plus a PKR 10,000 reactivation charge. Extended Study (after the 4th year, applicable to Batch 2020 onward): for 9 or more credit hours, pay the semester registration fee plus the credit hour fee; for less than 9 credit hours, pay only the credit hour fee. For AIT graduates (BE Tech - Civil, Electrical, Electronics): the admission fee (PKR 15,000) is waived and there is a 30% tuition fee discount in BS programs (Civil, Electrical, Electronics & Biomedical Engineering); the entry application fee is PKR 1,000 across all programs. For industrial employees and their children: the same admission fee waiver and 30% tuition discount apply (Civil, Electrical, Electronics), with the same PKR 1,000 entry application fee.
Sir Syed University of Engineering & Technology (SSUET) does not provide or operate an on-campus hostel or student housing facility.
